policy: vault42 1.0.0 ships as 100.00% of REACHABLE statements. This file is the
denominator's fine print: every statement listed here is uncovered on
purpose, and the release gate asserts covered + excluded == total against a
profile it also checks is the canonical one, so the set cannot grow, rot or
be measured against a smaller tree without someone noticing.
bucket B: reachable only by adding a production seam whose sole consumer
would be the test. Refused on design grounds, not on effort.
bucket C: unreachable, because a check earlier in the same call path
already excluded the input that would trigger it.
Rules. The count may only ever go down, and cov-gaps.py holds it as a
ratchet (BASELINE_MAX_ENTRIES) so a 39th entry fails the gate on its own.
The ratchet lives in the script rather than in this file on purpose: adding
an entry then has to be a two-file diff, and the second file is the one a
reviewer already reads. A new entry needs the same review as a security
change, and its justification must be checkable by reading the cited call
sites and nothing else. Deleting the branch outright always beats listing
it here: six statements that qualified were deleted rather than excluded
(the Nil branch in redis exec, the dead crypto/rand.Read error checks in
crypto/argon2.go and crypto/recovery.go, and the duplicate template compile
in email/preview.go). Two more entries were retired by testing them: the
key generation failure in keystore.Rotate, which a swapped reader does reach
under GODEBUG=cryptocustomrand=1, and the document ID failure in
servicedoc.Put, which reads through io.ReadFull and not crypto/rand.Read.
confirmed=false means the entry was identified by elimination against a
container-free profile, not measured: the DB-backed suites could not run
when the set was written. cov-gaps.py --verify-exclusions fails on any
unconfirmed entry, so one canonical scripts/coverage.sh run on a host with
a container runtime settles them.
line is advisory and occurrence is authoritative: source is the frozen
text, and occurrence says which identical line in the file it is. An entry
matches only when the occurrence-th line carrying its frozen text is the
line it names, so a refactor that leaves the same text on the same line by
coincidence does not satisfy it. The cost is that churn among the identical
lines above an entry fails the gate until the entry is re-reviewed, which is
the intended price of freezing text as unspecific as a bare return. Use
--relocate after a refactor moves a statement, then re-review the diff.
Verify:  python3 scripts/cov-gaps.py PROFILE --verify-exclusions
Measure: python3 scripts/cov-gaps.py PROFILE --exclude .coverage-exclusions.json

entries.justification: LoadConfig returns an error unless len(c.MasterKey) == 32 (cmd/admin-gateway/config.go:159) and main() dies on that error at main.go:66, long before this line. main.go:147 hands keystore.New a full-length copy of that key, append([]byte(nil), cfg.MasterKey...), and internal/keystore/keystore.go:128 holds keystore.New's only error return, the len(masterKey) != 32 check, so New cannot fail at this call site. Both legs are pinned by tests that fail if the reasoning stops holding: TestKeystoreNewHasExactlyOneErrorPath (cmd/admin-gateway/main_test.go:1186) fails if keystore.New grows a second error return or if its one return stops being guarded by the length check, and TestLoadConfigRequiredSettings/"master key must be 32 bytes" (cmd/admin-gateway/config_test.go:220) fails if LoadConfig stops refusing a short key. The child-process fixture cannot provoke it either: the master key reaches the binary only through MASTER_KEY_FILE, which LoadConfig validates before the process opens a database connection (TestConfigErrorIsFatalBeforeAnyDatabaseWork). The error is read rather than discarded on purpose, so a future second error path in keystore.New arrives here as a loud exit instead of a nil dereference on the next line.

log.Fatalf calls os.Exit(1), so this statement ends whatever process executes it before any assertion can run, and the canonical profile is a single `go test -coverprofile` run (cov_run in scripts/lib/coverage-env.sh) that never merges a re-executed child's counters. The condition is provokable and is already asserted where it is decided: TestLoadConfigRequiresBothUpstreams pins the error LoadConfig returns for each missing upstream. Covering main's reaction to it needs main split into a run() error whose only caller besides main would be the test.

The same os.Exit(1) as the config guard above it, on the NewBridge error. NewBridge (cmd/bridge/proxy.go:81) returns an error only when url.Parse rejects one of the two upstreams, which TestNewBridgeRejectsUnparseableUpstreams asserts directly on the constructor; what stays unexecuted here is only main's log.Fatalf reaction to it.

The third os.Exit(1), inside main's listener goroutine. srv.ListenAndServe returns a non-ErrServerClosed error only for a bind failure such as an address already in use, which a test can provoke but not survive: log.Fatalf ends the test binary before any assertion, and a child process re-executed to reach it contributes no counters to the canonical profile.

main's only statement is os.Exit, so any in-process test that reaches it terminates the test binary before the testing package writes the profile, and main.go offers no seam to intercept the exit: run's return value is passed straight to os.Exit. The wiring is executed and asserted, just not recorded. TestMainWiring in cmd/recover/main_test.go re-runs the test binary as the recover binary through the RECOVER_TEST_ARGS branch of TestMain, which calls main() directly, and checks the real process exit codes (0, 1, 2), that os.Args[1:] slicing lets flags reach the parser, and that stdout stays empty on every failing run. A child process's counters are never merged into the parent's -coverprofile, which testing writes from in-process counters at the end of m.Run(); confirmed empirically with a minimal module whose child ran main() with GOCOVERDIR set and still left both main and run at 0.0% in the parent's profile. Covering this would require a production seam (var exit = os.Exit) whose sole consumer is the test, which is bucket B.

bucket C. keystore.New has exactly one error return, `if len(masterKey) != 32`, and no other statement in it can fail: the rest is a copy and a struct literal. main.go:212 is the same length check on the same slice, four lines above the call, and it ends in log.Fatal, which calls os.Exit. Control therefore reaches keystore.New only with a masterKey proven to be 32 bytes, in straight-line single-goroutine code that cannot change it in between, so the constructor cannot return a non-nil error here. The guard itself is covered by TestKeyRotationDBRequiresA32ByteMasterKey (absent, too short, too long).

entries.source: log.Fatalf("admin-gateway: failed to parse layout template: %v", err)
entries.justification: template.ParseFS over the embedded templates/*.html, parsed by NewFrontendHandler at wiring time. A template that did not parse would take down every test binary that builds the gateway before any assertion ran, so the guard is a build-time assertion with no runtime input; and log.Fatalf calls os.Exit, so even a reachable failure leaves nothing in-process to observe.

entries.source: log.Fatalf("admin-gateway: failed to parse template %s: %v", page, err)
entries.justification: The per-page copy of the layout-template guard, same embed.FS and same log.Fatalf.

entries.source: return nil, fmt.Errorf("aes: new cipher: %w", err)
entries.justification: aes.NewCipher errors only for a key length outside {16,24,32}, and Encrypt returns early unless len(key) == 32.

entries.source: return nil, fmt.Errorf("aes: new gcm: %w", err)
entries.justification: cipher.NewGCM errors only for a block size other than 16, and the block came from a successful aes.NewCipher.

entries.source: return nil, fmt.Errorf("aes: new cipher: %w", err)
entries.justification: Decrypt's copy of the Encrypt guard, behind the same 32-byte key check.

entries.source: return nil, fmt.Errorf("aes: new gcm: %w", err)
entries.justification: Decrypt's copy of the Encrypt guard, on a block that came from a successful aes.NewCipher.

The fallback inside func init(). init runs before TestMain, so no test can install a HashPassword failure, and the only failure HashPassword has left is a 5s semaphore timeout on a semaphore nothing has touched yet.
pubKey came from parseJWKHeader, which admits only RSA 2048-4096 or a P-256/P-384 point it already validated with key.ECDH(). ComputeJWKThumbprint cannot fail on either.

entries.source: return "", fmt.Errorf("unexpected ecdh pub length %d", len(raw))
entries.justification: raw came from a successful ecdhPub.Bytes(), which is canonical SEC1 uncompressed by construction, so its length is fixed by the curve.

Bucket C. x509.MarshalPKIXPublicKey returns an error only for a key type it does not recognise, and KIDFromPublicKey takes *rsa.PublicKey, which it does. The fallback exists to keep the function total rather than to introduce an error return no caller could act on, and the comment above it says so. Reaching it would need the standard library to stop understanding RSA public keys.

entries.source: return nil, errors.New("recovery: wrapped key too large")
entries.justification: Self-documented gosec G115 guard: an RSA-OAEP ciphertext is exactly the modulus size, so exceeding math.MaxUint32 would need a 34-gigabit RSA key.
Reached only if the address has no @ or ends in one, after mail.ParseAddress already succeeded. RFC 5322 parsing guarantees both an @ and a non-empty domain.
json.Marshal of sendGridPayload, a struct of strings and string slices with no channels, funcs, cycles or MarshalJSON implementations.

entries.source: panic("email: failed to initialize default templates: " + err.Error())
entries.justification: func init() over an embed.FS. If those templates did not parse the binary would not start, so no test process can reach the panic.

json.Marshal(session), where session is the *webauthn.SessionData returned by BeginRegistration: strings, byte slices, a time, protocol enum strings, and one protocol.AuthenticationExtensions map. The map is the only member that could hold an unmarshalable value, and RegisterBegin passes no option to BeginRegistration, so nothing caller-supplied ever enters it.

Companion statement of the entry for webauthn.go:106; the block holds a WriteError and this return, and a partially named block is rejected. Both are the arm of a json.Marshal(session) that cannot fail: in go-webauthn v0.17.4 BeginRegistration builds SessionData from Challenge, RelyingPartyID, UserID, UserVerification, CredParams, Mediation and Expires only, all strings, byte slices, a time and enum strings. Extensions is the one member that could hold an unmarshalable value and BeginRegistration never assigns it. Verified against webauthn@v0.17.4/webauthn/registration.go:103-110 and types_session.go:32-43.
json.Marshal(session) for BeginLogin, the same *webauthn.SessionData as the registration path, and VerifyBegin passes it no option either.

Companion statement of the entry for webauthn.go:225, same block, same unreachable json.Marshal(session) arm. BeginLogin copies session.Extensions from assertion.Response.Extensions, which is only populated by a LoginOption applied in beginLogin's opts loop, and VerifyBegin calls BeginLogin with no options, so it stays nil. The remaining SessionData members are strings, byte slices, a time and enum strings. Verified against webauthn@v0.17.4/webauthn/login.go:79-132.
SerializeJWKSJSON is json.Marshal(SerializeJWKS(keys)) over a JWKS of pure strings. A nil *rsa.PublicKey in the map would panic in pub.N.Bytes(), not return an error, so no input takes this branch.
The return of the same unreachable json.Marshal failure as the WriteError above it.
rawRSToDER is asn1.Marshal of a struct of two non-negative *big.Int, which has no failure mode.
json.Marshal of a map[string]string literal built two lines above: no channels, funcs, cycles or MarshalJSON implementations, so the encoder has no failure mode to reach.

entries.source: return "", fmt.Errorf("keystore: marshal public key: %w", err)
entries.justification: x509.MarshalPKIXPublicKey on an *rsa.PublicKey fails in exactly one case: asn1.Marshal rejects a nil modulus. Import derives the kid first via KIDFromPublicKey, which calls pub.N.Bytes() and panics on a nil modulus, so no key reaches this line holding the only value that could fail it. Every other malformed key is refused two lines earlier by MarshalSigningKeyPEM, which keystore_marshal_failure_test.go demonstrates.

entries.source: return nil, fmt.Errorf("github userinfo: build emails request: %w", err)
entries.justification: In production emailsURL is a constant. Under the test override it is g.userInfoURL + "/emails", and the same g.userInfoURL already built a successful request earlier in the call. Appending a safe literal to a string that already parsed cannot introduce a control character, bad escape or bad port. Covering it needs a second override field that exists only for the test.

pgxpool.NewWithConfig returns an error only from puddle.NewPool, which fails only for MaxSize < 1. MaxConns comes from pgxpool.ParseConfig, which rejects pool_max_conns below 1 and otherwise defaults to max(4, NumCPU), and New overwrites it only when maxConns is in [1, 1000]. Every other field New sets is a constant duration. The dial itself is lazy, so an unreachable database surfaces at the Ping three lines below, which is covered.

entries.source: return nil, fmt.Errorf("honeypot: fake JWT: %w", err)
entries.justification: honeypot.GenerateFakeJWT fails only when honeypot.randRead fails, and randRead is an unexported package var that internal/service cannot reach. Covering it means injecting the honeypot generators into AuthService: a production seam on a decoy-credential path whose only consumer would be this test.

entries.source: return nil, fmt.Errorf("honeypot: fake refresh: %w", err)
entries.justification: The same seam as the fake-JWT branch above it, for the fake refresh token.

entries.source: return nil, fmt.Errorf("blob compress init: %w", err)
entries.justification: flate.NewWriter errors only for a level outside -2..9, and the call passes the constant flate.BestCompression.

entries.source: return nil, fmt.Errorf("blob compress write: %w", err)
entries.justification: The sink is a bytes.Buffer, whose Write never returns an error.

entries.source: return nil, fmt.Errorf("blob compress close: %w", err)
entries.justification: flate.Writer.Close surfaces only a sink error, and the sink is the same bytes.Buffer.

Bucket C. blobDataAAD errors only when the id contains a colon (blobAADSafeID). The id here is minted by vaultcrypto.RandomUUID six lines above, which formats hex digits and dashes, so no caller can reach this. The same helper's error return IS exercised where the id comes from a stored row, by TestBlobDownloadRefusesAStoredIDThatCollidesWithALabelAAD, so the guard is not dead code, only unreachable on the upload path.

Bucket C. blobLabelAAD errors on the same colon check, against the same freshly minted id as the entry above. Upload takes no id from the caller: Upload and UploadNamed both delegate to uploadInternal, which mints its own.

Bucket C. Redundant with the identical check at blob.go:239. decryptBlob calls blobDataAAD(blob.ID, pseudo) first and returns on error, and blobLabelAAD applies the same blobAADSafeID predicate to the same blob.ID, so a stored row whose id would fail here has already been refused. The guard is kept because the two AAD helpers are independent and a future caller may reach the label path without the data path.

entries.source: return fmt.Errorf("%w: dynamic not serializable", ErrInvalidProfile)
entries.justification: json.Marshal of a map[string]json.RawMessage in which every value already passed json.Valid.

checkRoles' self-documented defence-in-depth re-check. Reaching it needs a role that the loop above accepted, meaning !seed.ReservedAdminRoles[r], and that seed.FilterUserRoles then dropped. FilterUserRoles (seed/seed.go:75) drops exactly the roles for which ReservedAdminRoles[r] is true, so the two predicates are the same map lookup on the same slice and the lengths cannot differ. The early return above it means requested is never empty, which is FilterUserRoles' only other way to shorten the result.

The decode failure inside canonicalize. ValidateDocumentStructure ran first on the same bytes, walking the identical json.Decoder token stream with UseNumber and requiring a well-formed top-level object; Decode re-reads those bytes with the same scanner into map[string]any, which has no type-mismatch failure mode. A search over 8 million random JSON-ish inputs found no body the walk accepts and Decode rejects.

The trailing-content check inside canonicalize, which ValidateDocumentStructure already made at its own line 712 with the same errors.Is(err, io.EOF) test after the same top-level object. A body with a second document behind the first is rejected before canonicalize decodes anything, as TestPut_RejectsAnEmptyOrStructurallyInvalidBody demonstrates.

json.Encoder.Encode of the map[string]any that encoding/json itself just produced, into a bytes.Buffer whose Write never errors. The values can only be map, slice, string, bool, nil or json.Number, and a json.Number that came out of a successful decode always satisfies the encoder's isValidNumber check.

The non-string object key in walkDocObject. The loop is guarded by dec.More(), which is false when the next byte is '}', and in object-key position json.Decoder.Token returns either a string or an error for every other byte. So a token reaching this line with a nil error is always a string, and the malformed cases land on the err != nil branch above instead, as TestValidateDocumentStructure_RejectsAMalformedTokenStream shows for {"a":1,} and {1:2}.

The default arm of walkDocValue, reached only if Token returned a closing json.Delim in value position. walkDocValue is called from walkDocObject after a key, where a '}' or ']' is an error and not a token ({"a":} and {"a":]} both error), and from walkDocArray behind dec.More(), which is false before a ']'. Mismatched closers like {"a":[1} error on the closing Token at line 787 instead.
